newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols ease as bonds rally back.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols ease as bonds rally back.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options eased in late trade as the underlying fixed-income markets recouped most of their early losses, dealers said.
"We had a good rally back up," a trader at a bank affiliate at Chicago Board of Trade said. "Volatilities were up a little earlier, but we've been declining ever since (the rally began)."
Implied volatility for March T-bond futures options stood at around 9.3 percent just before the close, off marginally from late Tuesday levels.
A few huge futures purchases reversed sentiment in the CBOT pit, triggering a wave of shortcovering, the bank affiliate trader said, adding that options volume was moderate.
Traders expected volatilities to stay on a softer note for the rest of the week amid a dearth of heavy-weight economic data releases.
After a mixed bag of data in recent weeks, traders said the Federal Reserve was unlikely to raise interest rates at the Feb 4-5 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.

"Short-term interest-ratewise, I think everyone is pretty much content with moderate growth and, really, no core inflation," a Eurodollar trader for a brokerage firm at Chicago Mercantile Exchange said.
Overall producer and consumer prices for December recently released were on the high side of the market's expectations, but the "core" prices excluding food and energy were benign, he noted.
Implied volatility for CME June Eurodollar futures options stood at about 12.7 percent.
